1	# C ABI contract
2	
3	The grader loads `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so` with `dlopen` and drives it through
4	the C ABI below. The canonical header is `examples/abi/bonsai.h`; this document
5	defines the semantics the harness relies on.
6	
7	```c
8	typedef struct bonsai_model   bonsai_model;
9	typedef struct bonsai_context bonsai_context;
10	
11	uint32_t    bonsai_abi_version(void);       /* returns 1 */
12	const char *bonsai_last_error(void);        /* thread-local; NULL if none */
13	
14	int32_t  bonsai_model_open(const char *gguf_path, bonsai_model **out_model);
15	void     bonsai_model_close(bonsai_model *model);
16	int32_t  bonsai_n_vocab(const bonsai_model *model);
17	int32_t  bonsai_n_ctx_train(const bonsai_model *model);
18	
19	int32_t  bonsai_tokenize(const bonsai_model *model, const char *utf8,
20	                         int32_t add_bos, int32_t *ids, int32_t capacity);
21	
22	int32_t  bonsai_tensor_count(const bonsai_model *model);
23	int32_t  bonsai_tensor_info(const bonsai_model *model, int32_t index,
24	                            const char **name, int32_t *ggml_type,
25	                            int32_t *rank, int64_t ne[4]);
26	int64_t  bonsai_tensor_dequant(const bonsai_model *model, const char *name,
27	                               float *out, int64_t capacity);
28	
29	int32_t  bonsai_context_create(bonsai_model *model, int32_t n_ctx,
30	                               int32_t n_batch, bonsai_context **out_ctx);
31	void     bonsai_context_close(bonsai_context *ctx);
32	int32_t  bonsai_context_reset(bonsai_context *ctx);
33	int32_t  bonsai_eval(bonsai_context *ctx, const int32_t *tokens, int32_t n_tokens,
34	                     float *logits, int32_t logits_capacity);
35	int32_t  bonsai_generate_greedy(bonsai_context *ctx,
36	                                const int32_t *prompt, int32_t n_prompt,
37	                                int32_t n_predict, uint32_t flags,
38	                                int32_t *out_ids);
39	```
40	
41	## Build artifact
42	
43	- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` at the submission root must produce
44	  `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`.
45	- Symbols are C linkage (`extern "C"`), no C++ mangling, no extra shared
46	  libraries except the system Vulkan loader/libc. The grader checks that the
47	  library does not link llama.cpp/ggml.
48	- The library must be safe to `dlopen` without environment variables or files
49	  beside the GGUF path.
50	
51	## Model
52	
53	- `bonsai_model_open` parses the GGUF at `gguf_path`. It must not open any other
54	  model/weight file. The path is a normal filesystem path supplied by the
55	  harness.
56	- `bonsai_n_vocab` returns the vocabulary size from the GGUF tokenizer
57	  metadata.
58	- `bonsai_n_ctx_train` returns the model context length from the GGUF
59	  `context_length` metadata.
60	- Multiple models may be opened, but the tests normally use one.
61	- Errors: return a negative code and set a human-readable `bonsai_last_error`.
62	
63	## Tokenizer
64	
65	- `bonsai_tokenize` implements the model's tokenizer from the GGUF metadata:
66	  GPT-2 byte-level BPE with the `qwen35` pre-tokenizer described in
67	  `TOKENIZER.md`.
68	- `add_bos != 0` requests BOS insertion. This model's GGUF sets
69	  `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = false`, so the reference (`llama_tokenize`
70	  with `add_special = add_bos != 0`) does **not** prepend BOS even when
71	  `add_bos != 0`; the ids are the same as with `add_bos = 0`. The harness
72	  always calls with `add_bos = 0`.
73	- Special tokens contained in the GGUF vocabulary are matched atomically as
74	  their UTF-8 byte sequences. No chat template is applied.
75	- If `ids == NULL`, return the required number of ids without writing.
76	- If `ids != NULL` and `capacity < required`, return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
77	- The token stream must exactly match llama.cpp's tokenizer for the same flags.
78	
79	## Tensor introspection (staged tests)
80	
81	- `bonsai_tensor_count` returns the number of tensors in the GGUF.
82	- `bonsai_tensor_info` returns the tensor name (owned by the model), the numeric
83	  GGML type id (as reported by `gguf-py`), the rank, and `ne[0..3]` in **GGUF
84	  order** (`ne[0]` is the contiguous/inner dimension).
85	- `bonsai_tensor_dequant` writes the tensor to `out` as **f32** in PyTorch /
86	  safetensors row-major order: the GGUF dimensions are reversed, so `ne[0]`
87	  varies fastest and element `(i1, i0)` is at `i1*ne[0] + i0`.
88	- For PTQ1_0 the values must match the reference dequantization bit-exactly
89	  (no approximation tolerance is applied). For F32 tensors the values are
90	  copied bit-exactly.
91	- Returns the element count, or `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY` if `capacity` is too
92	  small.
93	
94	## Context and evaluation
95	
96	- `bonsai_context_create` allocates a context with `n_ctx` positions. `n_batch`
97	  is a processing hint; the engine may choose its own internal batching.
98	- `bonsai_context_reset` discards all KV/recurrent state and positions.
99	- `bonsai_eval` appends `n_tokens` token ids (n_tokens >= 1) and evaluates
100	  them. The token ids are already tokenized; the engine must not re-tokenize
101	  them.
102	- If `logits != NULL`, it must point to at least `n_vocab` floats; the engine
103	  writes the f32 logits for the **last token**. If `capacity < n_vocab`,
104	  return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
105	- The engine must support incremental calls: `bonsai_eval` on a prompt followed
106	  by repeated `bonsai_eval` with one token, producing the same state as one
107	  large call.
108	- Position indices advance by the number of tokens appended; reset starts at 0.
109	
110	## Greedy generation
111	
112	- `bonsai_generate_greedy` evaluates `prompt[0..n_prompt)` (may be empty), then
113	  selects the argmax token of the last-token logits, appends it, and repeats up
114	  to `n_predict` times.
115	- It writes generated token ids to `out_ids` (capacity at least `n_predict`) and
116	  returns the count. It stops early at the model's EOS token (from the GGUF
117	  tokenizer metadata) unless
118	  `BONSAI_GEN_IGNORE_EOS` is set.
119	- Determinism is required: same prompt and context size produce the same ids.
120	- After the call the context state is unspecified; the harness resets it.
121	
122	## Errors and robustness
123	
124	- `bonsai_last_error` returns a thread-local NUL-terminated string, valid until
125	  the next API call on that thread, or NULL.
126	- The library must not call `exit`, abort, or install signal handlers. Invalid
127	  arguments and allocation failures return negative codes.
128	- All API calls are made from one thread at a time. The engine may spawn worker
129	  threads internally; it must join/free them in `close`.

# C ABI contract

The grader loads `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so` with `dlopen` and drives it through
the C ABI below. The canonical header is `examples/abi/bonsai.h`; this document
defines the semantics the harness relies on.

```c
typedef struct bonsai_model   bonsai_model;
typedef struct bonsai_context bonsai_context;

uint32_t    bonsai_abi_version(void);       /* returns 1 */
const char *bonsai_last_error(void);        /* thread-local; NULL if none */

int32_t  bonsai_model_open(const char *gguf_path, bonsai_model **out_model);
void     bonsai_model_close(bonsai_model *model);
int32_t  bonsai_n_vocab(const bonsai_model *model);
int32_t  bonsai_n_ctx_train(const bonsai_model *model);

int32_t  bonsai_tokenize(const bonsai_model *model, const char *utf8,
                         int32_t add_bos, int32_t *ids, int32_t capacity);

int32_t  bonsai_tensor_count(const bonsai_model *model);
int32_t  bonsai_tensor_info(const bonsai_model *model, int32_t index,
                            const char **name, int32_t *ggml_type,
                            int32_t *rank, int64_t ne[4]);
int64_t  bonsai_tensor_dequant(const bonsai_model *model, const char *name,
                               float *out, int64_t capacity);

int32_t  bonsai_context_create(bonsai_model *model, int32_t n_ctx,
                               int32_t n_batch, bonsai_context **out_ctx);
void     bonsai_context_close(bonsai_context *ctx);
int32_t  bonsai_context_reset(bonsai_context *ctx);
int32_t  bonsai_eval(bonsai_context *ctx, const int32_t *tokens, int32_t n_tokens,
                     float *logits, int32_t logits_capacity);
int32_t  bonsai_generate_greedy(bonsai_context *ctx,
                                const int32_t *prompt, int32_t n_prompt,
                                int32_t n_predict, uint32_t flags,
                                int32_t *out_ids);
```

## Build artifact

- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` at the submission root must produce
  `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`.
- Symbols are C linkage (`extern "C"`), no C++ mangling, no extra shared
  libraries except the system Vulkan loader/libc. The grader checks that the
  library does not link llama.cpp/ggml.
- The library must be safe to `dlopen` without environment variables or files
  beside the GGUF path.

## Model

- `bonsai_model_open` parses the GGUF at `gguf_path`. It must not open any other
  model/weight file. The path is a normal filesystem path supplied by the
  harness.
- `bonsai_n_vocab` returns the vocabulary size from the GGUF tokenizer
  metadata.
- `bonsai_n_ctx_train` returns the model context length from the GGUF
  `context_length` metadata.
- Multiple models may be opened, but the tests normally use one.
- Errors: return a negative code and set a human-readable `bonsai_last_error`.

## Tokenizer

- `bonsai_tokenize` implements the model's tokenizer from the GGUF metadata:
  GPT-2 byte-level BPE with the `qwen35` pre-tokenizer described in
  `TOKENIZER.md`.
- `add_bos != 0` requests BOS insertion. This model's GGUF sets
  `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = false`, so the reference (`llama_tokenize`
  with `add_special = add_bos != 0`) does **not** prepend BOS even when
  `add_bos != 0`; the ids are the same as with `add_bos = 0`. The harness
  always calls with `add_bos = 0`.
- Special tokens contained in the GGUF vocabulary are matched atomically as
  their UTF-8 byte sequences. No chat template is applied.
- If `ids == NULL`, return the required number of ids without writing.
- If `ids != NULL` and `capacity < required`, return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
- The token stream must exactly match llama.cpp's tokenizer for the same flags.

## Tensor introspection (staged tests)

- `bonsai_tensor_count` returns the number of tensors in the GGUF.
- `bonsai_tensor_info` returns the tensor name (owned by the model), the numeric
  GGML type id (as reported by `gguf-py`), the rank, and `ne[0..3]` in **GGUF
  order** (`ne[0]` is the contiguous/inner dimension).
- `bonsai_tensor_dequant` writes the tensor to `out` as **f32** in PyTorch /
  safetensors row-major order: the GGUF dimensions are reversed, so `ne[0]`
  varies fastest and element `(i1, i0)` is at `i1*ne[0] + i0`.
- For PTQ1_0 the values must match the reference dequantization bit-exactly
  (no approximation tolerance is applied). For F32 tensors the values are
  copied bit-exactly.
- Returns the element count, or `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY` if `capacity` is too
  small.

## Context and evaluation

- `bonsai_context_create` allocates a context with `n_ctx` positions. `n_batch`
  is a processing hint; the engine may choose its own internal batching.
- `bonsai_context_reset` discards all KV/recurrent state and positions.
- `bonsai_eval` appends `n_tokens` token ids (n_tokens >= 1) and evaluates
  them. The token ids are already tokenized; the engine must not re-tokenize
  them.
- If `logits != NULL`, it must point to at least `n_vocab` floats; the engine
  writes the f32 logits for the **last token**. If `capacity < n_vocab`,
  return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
- The engine must support incremental calls: `bonsai_eval` on a prompt followed
  by repeated `bonsai_eval` with one token, producing the same state as one
  large call.
- Position indices advance by the number of tokens appended; reset starts at 0.

## Greedy generation

- `bonsai_generate_greedy` evaluates `prompt[0..n_prompt)` (may be empty), then
  selects the argmax token of the last-token logits, appends it, and repeats up
  to `n_predict` times.
- It writes generated token ids to `out_ids` (capacity at least `n_predict`) and
  returns the count. It stops early at the model's EOS token (from the GGUF
  tokenizer metadata) unless
  `BONSAI_GEN_IGNORE_EOS` is set.
- Determinism is required: same prompt and context size produce the same ids.
- After the call the context state is unspecified; the harness resets it.

## Errors and robustness

- `bonsai_last_error` returns a thread-local NUL-terminated string, valid until
  the next API call on that thread, or NULL.
- The library must not call `exit`, abort, or install signal handlers. Invalid
  arguments and allocation failures return negative codes.
- All API calls are made from one thread at a time. The engine may spawn worker
  threads internally; it must join/free them in `close`.

1	# Task: a Vulkan inference engine for Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B
2	
3	Implement **`bonsai-vk`**, a Vulkan inference engine for the model in
4	`data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0.gguf`, written in **Zig 0.17.0** using
5	**Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0**.
6	
7	The engine must load the GGUF file at runtime, reproduce the model's logits and
8	greedy token sequence, and be as fast as possible on the provided AMD GPU.
9	`ref/` contains symbol-stripped llama.cpp binaries with CPU and Vulkan backends
10	and a reference runner; use them as the correctness oracle. `data/` also
11	contains the dequantized weights as a safetensors file for development.
12	
13	## Deliverable
14	
15	A Zig project at the root of this directory that builds offline with:
16	
17	```
18	zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
19	```
20	
21	and produces **`zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`** exporting exactly the C ABI in
22	`ABI.md` (`extern "C"`, no C++ mangling, no extra required runtime files).
23	
24	The library must be self-contained:
25	
26	- It reads only the GGUF path passed by the harness. It must not read the
27	  safetensors file, a converted sidecar, or any other model file at runtime.
28	- It must not embed model weights or precomputed results in the submission.
29	- It must not link to or execute llama.cpp/ggml, or any prebuilt inference
30	  engine. All model computation must go through Vulkan compute shaders; the
31	  definition of model computation and the CPU allowlist are under Target and
32	  constraints.
33	- No network access is available. The build must not fetch dependencies.
34	- The grading build runs in a clean container containing only the files you
35	  submit. `data/`, `docs/` and `ref/` are not present at build time; do not
36	  read them from `build.zig` or embed them, and do not hard-code `/workspace`
37	  paths. Anything the build needs must live in the submission.
38	
39	## Environment
40	
41	Everything is offline. Available tools and data:
42	
43	- **Zig 0.17.0** on `PATH` (`zig`). Note that `@cImport` is not available in
44	  this Zig version; `zig translate-c` is.
45	- **Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0**: headers, loader, `glslc`, `glslangValidator`,
46	  `slangc`, `spirv-*`, `vulkaninfo`, validation layers, `vkprofiles`.
47	- **Python** with `numpy`, `safetensors`, and the fork's `gguf-py` reader. It is
48	  importable as `import gguf` from the default `python`; `PYTHONPATH` is preset
49	  (`python -I` ignores it and will not find the module). `gguf-py` can parse
50	  this GGUF and expose the raw tensor bytes and metadata; it has no PTQ1_0
51	  dequantizer and no runtime tokenizer.
52	- **Data**: `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0.gguf` (the model),
53	  `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0-f16.safetensors` (dequantized weights),
54	  and `data/samples/` (sample prompts/corpus). `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` gives
55	  reference token ids for visible strings.
56	- **Reference**: `ref/bin/{llama-cli,llama-debug,llama-perplexity,bonsai-ref,bonsai-ref-cpu}`
57	  are stripped llama.cpp builds. `-ngl 0` / `-ngl 99` or `ctx ... cpu|vulkan`
58	  select the backend; `bonsai-ref-cpu` has no Vulkan backend. The Vulkan backend
59	  runs at roughly 130–180 token/s generation and 2,600–3,500 token/s prefill on
60	  this GPU; the CPU backend is memory-bandwidth-bound at roughly 10–35 token/s,
61	  so reserve it for tokenizer checks and short spot checks. `ref/PROTOCOL.md`
62	  describes the line protocol.
63	- **Reference use — black box.** Run the reference binaries through their
64	  documented CLI and line protocol only. Do **not** disassemble, decompile,
65	  debug, or otherwise analyze the binaries, and do not read them with `strings`,
66	  `nm`, `readelf`, `objdump`, `llvm-objdump`, `gdb`, `lldb`, custom ELF parsers
67	  or disassembler bindings; do not link to or reuse their code. Recover the
68	  architecture from the GGUF, the safetensors development copy and the
69	  documented runner output. Treating `ref/bin` as anything other than a
70	  black-box oracle is non-compliant.
71	- **Docs**: `docs/` contains the Vulkan 1.4 spec, Roadmap 2026 appendix and
72	  profile, SPIR-V/GLSL specs, GGUF spec, Vulkan Profiles overview, and Zig docs.
73	
74	## Bash command classification
75	
76	Claude Code may deny a safe Bash command when it is compound. Prefer one simple
77	command per call, do not set environment variables to paths outside the
78	workspace, and if a command is still denied, put it in a workspace script and
79	run the script.
80	
81	## Time budget
82	
83	The session is terminated at a fixed wall-clock deadline. `BENCH_DEADLINE_EPOCH`
84	holds the deadline as Unix time, and `time-left` prints the remaining time. The
85	default budget is 2 hours; trust the environment variable if it differs.
86	
87	Only files in this workspace at the deadline are graded. The conversation is
88	not saved for grading, so write code, run tests and update `NOTES.md`
89	continuously rather than leaving everything to the end. Plan the budget: the
90	Vulkan reference is fast enough for frequent checks, the CPU reference is slow,
91	and hidden grading uses precomputed CPU values, so CPU inference is never
92	required.
93	
94	## Target and constraints
95	
96	- Target **Vulkan 1.4** and the compute-relevant Vulkan Roadmap 2026 feature
97	  subset in `DEVICE.md`. The GPU does not support three non-compute Roadmap 2026
98	  items (presentation/copy/host-image); those are not required.
99	- The engine must create a Vulkan device from the provided GPU and run the
100	  model's forward pass on it. **Model computation** means every arithmetic
101	  operation on model weights or activations in the forward pass, including
102	  normalization, activations (silu/sigmoid), softmax, RoPE, the GDN
103	  recurrence, conv1d, KV-cache updates and projections. All of it must be
104	  issued as Vulkan compute work. CPU code is limited to tokenization, Vulkan
105	  command/memory orchestration and I/O; CPU tensor arithmetic is a violation,
106	  including a CPU fallback used when Vulkan initialization fails (fail
107	  instead). A submission that performs model computation on the CPU is
108	  non-compliant even if it passes correctness and the VRAM residency gate.
109	- Support at least `n_ctx = 16384`; the harness creates contexts up to 16384
110	  (the long greedy case and the VRAM measurement). The model's training context
111	  is 262144.
112	- The harness calls the ABI single-threaded; the engine may use its own worker
113	  threads. Calls must not crash on malformed input; return a negative error and
114	  set `bonsai_last_error()`.
115	- Model execution must be deterministic for a fixed token sequence (greedy,
116	  no sampling randomness).
117	
118	## Correctness and scoring
119	
120	Correctness is the primary acceptance criterion; it is measured against
121	precomputed CPU llama.cpp golden values, using the same methodology as the
122	reference CPU-vs-Vulkan comparison (tokenizer IDs, dequantized tensors, logits,
123	per-position agreement, greedy tokens). Grading does not run CPU inference.
124	Performance is the optimization target; VRAM is a secondary acceptance gate. The
125	exact metrics and reference thresholds are in `ACCEPTANCE.md`. Hidden tests use
126	prompts and corpora not present here.
127	
128	Do not modify `data/`, `docs/`, or `ref/`.
129	
130	When done, leave `NOTES.md` with your design, known limitations, and measured
131	results.
132

# Task: a Vulkan inference engine for Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B

  `nm`, `readelf`, `objdump`, `llvm-objdump`, `gdb`, `lldb`, custom ELF parsers
  or disassembler bindings; do not link to or reuse their code. Recover the
  architecture from the GGUF, the safetensors development copy and the
  documented runner output. Treating `ref/bin` as anything other than a
  black-box oracle is non-compliant.
- **Docs**: `docs/` contains the Vulkan 1.4 spec, Roadmap 2026 appendix and
  profile, SPIR-V/GLSL specs, GGUF spec, Vulkan Profiles overview, and Zig docs.

## Bash command classification

Claude Code may deny a safe Bash command when it is compound. Prefer one simple
command per call, do not set environment variables to paths outside the
workspace, and if a command is still denied, put it in a workspace script and
run the script.

## Time budget

The session is terminated at a fixed wall-clock deadline. `BENCH_DEADLINE_EPOCH`
holds the deadline as Unix time, and `time-left` prints the remaining time. The
default budget is 2 hours; trust the environment variable if it differs.

Only files in this workspace at the deadline are graded. The conversation is
not saved for grading, so write code, run tests and update `NOTES.md`
continuously rather than leaving everything to the end. Plan the budget: the
Vulkan reference is fast enough for frequent checks, the CPU reference is slow,
and hidden grading uses precomputed CPU values, so CPU inference is never
required.

## Target and constraints

- Target **Vulkan 1.4** and the compute-relevant Vulkan Roadmap 2026 feature
  subset in `DEVICE.md`. The GPU does not support three non-compute Roadmap 2026
  items (presentation/copy/host-image); those are not required.
- The engine must create a Vulkan device from the provided GPU and run the
  model's forward pass on it. **Model computation** means every arithmetic
  operation on model weights or activations in the forward pass, including
  normalization, activations (silu/sigmoid), softmax, RoPE, the GDN
  recurrence, conv1d, KV-cache updates and projections. All of it must be
  issued as Vulkan compute work. CPU code is limited to tokenization, Vulkan
  command/memory orchestration and I/O; CPU tensor arithmetic is a violation,
  including a CPU fallback used when Vulkan initialization fails (fail
  instead). A submission that performs model computation on the CPU is
  non-compliant even if it passes correctness and the VRAM residency gate.
- Support at least `n_ctx = 16384`; the harness creates contexts up to 16384
  (the long greedy case and the VRAM measurement). The model's training context
  is 262144.
- The harness calls the ABI single-threaded; the engine may use its own worker
  threads. Calls must not crash on malformed input; return a negative error and
  set `bonsai_last_error()`.
- Model execution must be deterministic for a fixed token sequence (greedy,
  no sampling randomness).

## Correctness and scoring

Correctness is the primary acceptance criterion; it is measured against
precomputed CPU llama.cpp golden values, using the same methodology as the
reference CPU-vs-Vulkan comparison (tokenizer IDs, dequantized tensors, logits,
per-position agreement, greedy tokens). Grading does not run CPU inference.
Performance is the optimization target; VRAM is a secondary acceptance gate. The
exact metrics and reference thresholds are in `ACCEPTANCE.md`. Hidden tests use
prompts and corpora not present here.

Do not modify `data/`, `docs/`, or `ref/`.

When done, leave `NOTES.md` with your design, known limitations, and measured
results.

3	The GGUF contains the complete tokenizer dictionary and configuration:
4	
5	| key | value |
6	|---|---|
7	| `tokenizer.ggml.model` | `gpt2` |
8	| `tokenizer.ggml.pre` | `qwen35` |
9	| `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` | 248,320 strings |
10	| `tokenizer.ggml.merges` | 247,587 merge rules |
11	| `tokenizer.ggml.token_type` | 248,320 type codes |
12	| `tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id` | 248044 |
13	| `tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id` | 248046 |
14	| `tokenizer.ggml.padding_token_id` | 248044 |
15	| `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token` | false |
16	| `tokenizer.chat_template` | Jinja template (not used by the ABI) |
17	
18	This is a **GPT-2 byte-level BPE** tokenizer, not SentencePiece. The dictionary
19	and merges come from the GGUF; the missing details are the byte mapping and the
20	`qwen35` pre-tokenization rule.
21	
22	## 1. Byte-to-unicode mapping
23	
24	Map each raw byte to a printable Unicode code point (the standard GPT-2 table):
25	
26	```python
27	bs = list(range(ord("!"), ord("~") + 1)) + \
28	     list(range(ord("¡"), ord("¬") + 1)) + \
29	     list(range(ord("®"), ord("ÿ") + 1))
30	cs = bs[:]
31	n = 0
32	for b in range(256):
33	    if b not in bs:
34	        bs.append(b)
35	        cs.append(256 + n)
36	        n += 1
37	byte_to_unicode = {b: chr(c) for b, c in zip(bs, cs)}
38	```
39	
40	Tokens in the GGUF are already strings in this representation (for example a
41	leading space is `Ġ`). Merges are two such strings separated by a space.
42	
43	## 2. Pre-tokenization (`qwen35`)
44	
45	Before BPE, split the UTF-8-decoded text with this regex (equivalent to the
46	case-insensitive original used by the tokenizer):
47	
48	```
49	(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|'[rR][eE]|'[vV][eE]|'[mM]|'[lL][lL]|'[dD])
50	|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{L}\p{M}]+
51	|\p{N}
52	| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*
53	|\s*[\r\n]+
54	|\s+(?!\S)
55	|\s+
56	```
57	
58	This is the `qwen35` rule: letters may include combining marks (`\p{M}`),
59	unlike the older Qwen2 rule. `clean_spaces = false`: do not strip leading
60	spaces from the pre-tokenized pieces.
61	
62	## 3. BPE merges
63	
64	For each pre-token:
65	
66	1. Convert its raw UTF-8 bytes to the byte-to-unicode string.
67	2. Split into individual symbols.
68	3. Repeatedly merge the adjacent pair whose concatenation has the **lowest
69	   index** in `tokenizer.ggml.merges` (the list order is the merge rank), until
70	   no pair is present. Ties are resolved by the leftmost occurrence.
71	4. Map each resulting symbol to its index in `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`; that index
72	   is the token id.
73	
74	The merges are the usual `"left right"` strings, e.g. `Ġ Ġ` or `i n`. There are
75	247,587 entries; token id 0 is the first entry of the tokens array.
76	
77	## 4. Special tokens and BOS
78	
79	- Tokens whose type marks them as control/user-defined/special are matched
80	  **atomically** in the input text before BPE (e.g. `<|im_start|>`); they are
81	  emitted as their exact token ids.
82	- `add_bos_token` is false in the GGUF. The reference passes
83	  `add_special = (add_bos != 0)` to llama.cpp, which honors this metadata, so

85	  `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` is therefore identical to `ids`. The harness uses
86	  `add_bos = 0`.
87	- EOS is 248046; padding is 248044.
88	- The ABI does not apply the chat template. The harness tokenizes raw text and
89	  compares token ids with the reference tokenizer.
90	
91	## 5. Validation
92

94	reference ids for arbitrary strings. `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` in this directory

97	contains a few visible sample texts; hidden tests use different strings,

99	
100	The tokenizer is part of the correctness score (exact token ids). The dequant,
101	forward-pass and generation suites use token ids supplied by the harness, so a
102	tokenizer bug does not hide an inference bug.

three missing items are presentation/copy/host-image features that a headless
inference engine does not need.

The line-rasterization requirement is an OR-group; the device satisfies it via
rectangular/Bresenham/smooth/stippled-Bresenham. The required 2026 limits are
all met.

## Required compute feature set (all supported)

Core Vulkan 1.4 features, including:

- `shaderFloat16`, `shaderInt8`
- `storageBuffer16BitAccess`, `storageBuffer8BitAccess`
- `shaderIntegerDotProduct` (8-bit paths accelerated)
- `timelineSemaphore`, `bufferDeviceAddress`, `descriptorIndexing`
- `scalarBlockLayout`, `vulkanMemoryModel`

- `VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix` (revision 2; compute stage;
  `cooperativeMatrix = true`)
- `VK_KHR_maintenance5`, `VK_KHR_maintenance7`, `VK_KHR_maintenance8`,
  `VK_KHR_maintenance9`

- `VK_KHR_workgroup_memory_explicit_layout`

  `nullDescriptor`)
- `VK_KHR_pipeline_binary`, `VK_KHR_map_memory2`
- `VK_KHR_shader_clock`, `VK_KHR_compute_shader_derivatives`

1	# Reference runner protocol
2	
3	`ref/bin/bonsai-ref` is a symbol-stripped llama.cpp runner (CPU and Vulkan
4	backends) for the benchmark model. It reads one command per line on stdin and
5	replies with exactly one line on stdout.
6	
7	```
8	load <model.gguf>
9	info
10	tokenize <hex-utf8> [add_bos]
11	ctx <id> <n_ctx> <cpu|vulkan>
12	reset <id>
13	eval <id> <n_tokens> <token_id>...
14	logits <id> <output.bin>
15	gen <id> <n_predict> [ignore_eos]
16	quit
17	```
18	
19	| command | reply |
20	|---|---|
21	| `load <path>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
22	| `info` | `ok arch=<arch> n_layer=<n> n_embd=<n> n_vocab=<n> n_ctx_train=<n>` |
23	| `tokenize <hex> [1]` | `ok <n> <id>...` / `error <msg>` |
24	| `ctx <id> <n_ctx> <cpu\|vulkan>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
25	| `reset <id>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
26	| `eval <id> <n> <id>...` | `ok` / `error <msg>` (appends and evaluates) |
27	| `logits <id> <path>` | `ok <n_vocab>`; writes raw little-endian f32 logits for the last token |
28	| `gen <id> <n> [1]` | `ok <n_generated> <id>...` (greedy; stops at EOS unless the last argument is `1`) |
29	| `quit` | exits |
30	
31	Notes:
32	
33	- `<hex-utf8>` is the lowercase hex encoding of the UTF-8 text. This avoids
34	  quoting issues. Example: `tokenize 48656c6c6f` for `Hello`.
35	- `tokenize` uses the model's `qwen35` tokenizer; `add_bos` defaults to 0.
36	- `ctx` creates a context with `n_ctx` positions. `cpu` uses `-ngl 0`;
37	  `vulkan` uses the Vulkan backend with all layers offloaded.
38	- `eval` token ids are appended to the context in order; the context must have
39	  room. Call `reset` between independent prompts.
40	- `logits` writes `n_vocab` float32 values in model-vocabulary order.
41	- `gen` selects argmax at each step and appends the token; no sampling
42	  parameters.
43	- All state is deterministic for a fixed sequence.
44	- The CPU backend is memory-bandwidth-bound on this machine: expect tens of
45	  tokens/s, versus hundreds on the Vulkan backend (and thousands for prefill).
46	  Use `cpu` for tokenizer, metadata and short spot checks; use `vulkan` for
47	  iteration. The grader compares against precomputed CPU golden values, so you
48	  do not need to run CPU inference to be graded.
49	- `ref/bin/bonsai-ref-cpu` is the same runner built without the Vulkan backend;
50	  it accepts only `cpu` contexts and is useful for pure-CPU checks.
51	
52	`llama-cli`, `llama-debug` and `llama-perplexity` are also provided for
53	ad-hoc reference runs; `llama-cli -ngl 0` uses the CPU backend and
54	`llama-cli -ngl 99` the Vulkan backend.

1	# Task: a Vulkan inference engine for Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B
2	
3	Implement **`bonsai-vk`**, a Vulkan inference engine for the model in
4	`data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0.gguf`, written in **Zig 0.17.0** using
5	**Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0**.
6	
7	The engine must load the GGUF file at runtime, reproduce the model's logits and
8	greedy token sequence, and be as fast as possible on the provided AMD GPU.
9	`ref/` contains symbol-stripped llama.cpp binaries with CPU and Vulkan backends
10	and a reference runner; use them as the correctness oracle. `data/` also
11	contains the dequantized weights as a safetensors file for development.
12	
13	## Deliverable
14	
15	A Zig project at the root of this directory that builds offline with:
16	
17	```
18	zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
19	```
20	
21	and produces **`zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`** exporting exactly the C ABI in
22	`ABI.md` (`extern "C"`, no C++ mangling, no extra required runtime files).
23	
24	The library must be self-contained:
25	
26	- It reads only the GGUF path passed by the harness. It must not read the
27	  safetensors file, a converted sidecar, or any other model file at runtime.
28	- It must not embed model weights or precomputed results in the submission.
29	- It must not link to or execute llama.cpp/ggml, or any prebuilt inference
30	  engine. All model computation must go through Vulkan compute shaders; the
31	  definition of model computation and the CPU allowlist are under Target and
32	  constraints.
33	- No network access is available. The build must not fetch dependencies.
34	- The grading build runs in a clean container containing only the files you
35	  submit. `data/`, `docs/` and `ref/` are not present at build time; do not
36	  read them from `build.zig` or embed them, and do not hard-code `/workspace`
37	  paths. Anything the build needs must live in the submission.
38	
39	## Environment
40	
41	Everything is offline. Available tools and data:
42	
43	- **Zig 0.17.0** on `PATH` (`zig`). Note that `@cImport` is not available in
44	  this Zig version; `zig translate-c` is.
45	- **Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0**: headers, loader, `glslc`, `glslangValidator`,
46	  `slangc`, `spirv-*`, `vulkaninfo`, validation layers, `vkprofiles`.
47	- **Python** with `numpy`, `safetensors`, and the fork's `gguf-py` reader. It is
48	  importable as `import gguf` from the default `python`; `PYTHONPATH` is preset
49	  (`python -I` ignores it and will not find the module). `gguf-py` can parse
50	  this GGUF and expose the raw tensor bytes and metadata; it has no PTQ1_0
51	  dequantizer and no runtime tokenizer.
52	- **Data**: `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0.gguf` (the model),
53	  `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0-f16.safetensors` (dequantized weights),
54	  and `data/samples/` (sample prompts/corpus). `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` gives
55	  reference token ids for visible strings.
56	- **Reference**: `ref/bin/{llama-cli,llama-debug,llama-perplexity,bonsai-ref,bonsai-ref-cpu}`
57	  are stripped llama.cpp builds. `-ngl 0` / `-ngl 99` or `ctx ... cpu|vulkan`
58	  select the backend; `bonsai-ref-cpu` has no Vulkan backend. The Vulkan backend
59	  runs at roughly 130–180 token/s generation and 2,600–3,500 token/s prefill on
60	  this GPU; the CPU backend is memory-bandwidth-bound at roughly 10–35 token/s,
61	  so reserve it for tokenizer checks and short spot checks. `ref/PROTOCOL.md`
62	  describes the line protocol.
63	- **Reference use — black box.** Run the reference binaries through their
64	  documented CLI and line protocol only. Do **not** disassemble, decompile,
65	  debug, or otherwise analyze the binaries, and do not read them with `strings`,
66	  `nm`, `readelf`, `objdump`, `llvm-objdump`, `gdb`, `lldb`, custom ELF parsers
67	  or disassembler bindings; do not link to or reuse their code. Recover the
68	  architecture from the GGUF, the safetensors development copy and the
69	  documented runner output. Treating `ref/bin` as anything other than a
70	  black-box oracle is non-compliant.
71	- **Docs**: `docs/` contains the Vulkan 1.4 spec, Roadmap 2026 appendix and
72	  profile, SPIR-V/GLSL specs, GGUF spec, Vulkan Profiles overview, and Zig docs.
73	
74	## Bash command classification
75	
76	Claude Code may deny a safe Bash command when it is compound. Prefer one simple
77	command per call, do not set environment variables to paths outside the
78	workspace, and if a command is still denied, put it in a workspace script and
79	run the script.
80	
81	## Time budget
82	
83	The session is terminated at a fixed wall-clock deadline. `BENCH_DEADLINE_EPOCH`
84	holds the deadline as Unix time, and `time-left` prints the remaining time. The
85	default budget is 2 hours; trust the environment variable if it differs.
86	
87	Only files in this workspace at the deadline are graded. The conversation is
88	not saved for grading, so write code, run tests and update `NOTES.md`
89	continuously rather than leaving everything to the end. Plan the budget: the
90	Vulkan reference is fast enough for frequent checks, the CPU reference is slow,
91	and hidden grading uses precomputed CPU values, so CPU inference is never
92	required.
93	
94	## Target and constraints
95	
96	- Target **Vulkan 1.4** and the compute-relevant Vulkan Roadmap 2026 feature
97	  subset in `DEVICE.md`. The GPU does not support three non-compute Roadmap 2026
98	  items (presentation/copy/host-image); those are not required.
99	- The engine must create a Vulkan device from the provided GPU and run the
100	  model's forward pass on it. **Model computation** means every arithmetic
101	  operation on model weights or activations in the forward pass, including
102	  normalization, activations (silu/sigmoid), softmax, RoPE, the GDN
103	  recurrence, conv1d, KV-cache updates and projections. All of it must be
104	  issued as Vulkan compute work. CPU code is limited to tokenization, Vulkan
105	  command/memory orchestration and I/O; CPU tensor arithmetic is a violation,
106	  including a CPU fallback used when Vulkan initialization fails (fail
107	  instead). A submission that performs model computation on the CPU is
108	  non-compliant even if it passes correctness and the VRAM residency gate.
109	- Support at least `n_ctx = 16384`; the harness creates contexts up to 16384
110	  (the long greedy case and the VRAM measurement). The model's training context
111	  is 262144.
112	- The harness calls the ABI single-threaded; the engine may use its own worker
113	  threads. Calls must not crash on malformed input; return a negative error and
114	  set `bonsai_last_error()`.
115	- Model execution must be deterministic for a fixed token sequence (greedy,
116	  no sampling randomness).
117	
118	## Correctness and scoring
119	
120	Correctness is the primary acceptance criterion; it is measured against
121	precomputed CPU llama.cpp golden values, using the same methodology as the
122	reference CPU-vs-Vulkan comparison (tokenizer IDs, dequantized tensors, logits,
123	per-position agreement, greedy tokens). Grading does not run CPU inference.
124	Performance is the optimization target; VRAM is a secondary acceptance gate. The
125	exact metrics and reference thresholds are in `ACCEPTANCE.md`. Hidden tests use
126	prompts and corpora not present here.
127	
128	Do not modify `data/`, `docs/`, or `ref/`.
129	
130	When done, leave `NOTES.md` with your design, known limitations, and measured
131	results.
132

1	# Tokenizer specification
2	
3	The GGUF contains the complete tokenizer dictionary and configuration:
4	
5	| key | value |
6	|---|---|
7	| `tokenizer.ggml.model` | `gpt2` |
8	| `tokenizer.ggml.pre` | `qwen35` |
9	| `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` | 248,320 strings |
10	| `tokenizer.ggml.merges` | 247,587 merge rules |
11	| `tokenizer.ggml.token_type` | 248,320 type codes |
12	| `tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id` | 248044 |
13	| `tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id` | 248046 |
14	| `tokenizer.ggml.padding_token_id` | 248044 |
15	| `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token` | false |
16	| `tokenizer.chat_template` | Jinja template (not used by the ABI) |
17	
18	This is a **GPT-2 byte-level BPE** tokenizer, not SentencePiece. The dictionary
19	and merges come from the GGUF; the missing details are the byte mapping and the
20	`qwen35` pre-tokenization rule.
21	
22	## 1. Byte-to-unicode mapping
23	
24	Map each raw byte to a printable Unicode code point (the standard GPT-2 table):
25	
26	```python
27	bs = list(range(ord("!"), ord("~") + 1)) + \
28	     list(range(ord("¡"), ord("¬") + 1)) + \
29	     list(range(ord("®"), ord("ÿ") + 1))
30	cs = bs[:]
31	n = 0
32	for b in range(256):
33	    if b not in bs:
34	        bs.append(b)
35	        cs.append(256 + n)
36	        n += 1
37	byte_to_unicode = {b: chr(c) for b, c in zip(bs, cs)}
38	```
39	
40	Tokens in the GGUF are already strings in this representation (for example a
41	leading space is `Ġ`). Merges are two such strings separated by a space.
42	
43	## 2. Pre-tokenization (`qwen35`)
44	
45	Before BPE, split the UTF-8-decoded text with this regex (equivalent to the
46	case-insensitive original used by the tokenizer):
47	
48	```
49	(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|'[rR][eE]|'[vV][eE]|'[mM]|'[lL][lL]|'[dD])
50	|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{L}\p{M}]+
51	|\p{N}
52	| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*
53	|\s*[\r\n]+
54	|\s+(?!\S)
55	|\s+
56	```
57	
58	This is the `qwen35` rule: letters may include combining marks (`\p{M}`),
59	unlike the older Qwen2 rule. `clean_spaces = false`: do not strip leading
60	spaces from the pre-tokenized pieces.
61	
62	## 3. BPE merges
63	
64	For each pre-token:
65	
66	1. Convert its raw UTF-8 bytes to the byte-to-unicode string.
67	2. Split into individual symbols.
68	3. Repeatedly merge the adjacent pair whose concatenation has the **lowest
69	   index** in `tokenizer.ggml.merges` (the list order is the merge rank), until
70	   no pair is present. Ties are resolved by the leftmost occurrence.
71	4. Map each resulting symbol to its index in `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`; that index
72	   is the token id.
73	
74	The merges are the usual `"left right"` strings, e.g. `Ġ Ġ` or `i n`. There are
75	247,587 entries; token id 0 is the first entry of the tokens array.
76	
77	## 4. Special tokens and BOS
78	
79	- Tokens whose type marks them as control/user-defined/special are matched
80	  **atomically** in the input text before BPE (e.g. `<|im_start|>`); they are
81	  emitted as their exact token ids.
82	- `add_bos_token` is false in the GGUF. The reference passes
83	  `add_special = (add_bos != 0)` to llama.cpp, which honors this metadata, so
84	  `add_bos` does **not** prepend BOS for this model; `ids_add_bos` in
85	  `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` is therefore identical to `ids`. The harness uses
86	  `add_bos = 0`.
87	- EOS is 248046; padding is 248044.
88	- The ABI does not apply the chat template. The harness tokenizes raw text and
89	  compares token ids with the reference tokenizer.
90	
91	## 5. Validation
92	
93	`ref/bin/bonsai-ref` and `llama-cli` use the same tokenizer; use them to obtain
94	reference ids for arbitrary strings. `TOKENIZER-VECTORS.json` in this directory
95	lists reference ids for 15 visible strings (`ids_add_bos` is shown for
96	completeness and is identical to `ids` for this model). `data/samples/`
97	contains a few visible sample texts; hidden tests use different strings,
98	including Unicode, combining marks, code, whitespace and special tokens.
99	
100	The tokenizer is part of the correctness score (exact token ids). The dequant,
101	forward-pass and generation suites use token ids supplied by the harness, so a
102	tokenizer bug does not hide an inference bug.
103

1	# Model: Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B (`qwen35`)
2	
3	The model is `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0.gguf`. Its GGUF metadata and
4	tensor inventory are the source of truth for dimensions, tensor names, shapes
5	and quantization types; parse them with the provided `gguf-py` reader or
6	directly.
7	
8	**This document intentionally does not describe the architecture.** The layer
9	structure, tensor ordering, weight representation and numerical behavior are
10	part of the task. Recover them from the GGUF, the dequantized development
11	tensors in `data/Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B-PTQ1_0-f16.safetensors` (development only;
12	never read at runtime), and the reference runner.
13	
14	`ref/bin/bonsai-ref` is the numerical oracle; `ref/PROTOCOL.md` documents its
15	line protocol. Where your interpretation disagrees with the oracle, the oracle
16	wins.
17	
18	Contract notes:
19	
20	- The engine loads the GGUF at runtime and derives every weight from it; it must
21	  not read the safetensors file, embed weights, or use another engine.
22	- `bonsai_tensor_dequant` must match the reference dequantization exactly.
23	  Logits, per-position agreement and greedy tokens are scored against the CPU
24	  oracle (`ABI.md`, `ACCEPTANCE.md`).
25	- The ABI and context semantics are in `ABI.md`; the tokenizer is specified in
26	  `TOKENIZER.md`.
27

1	# C ABI contract
2	
3	The grader loads `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so` with `dlopen` and drives it through
4	the C ABI below. The canonical header is `examples/abi/bonsai.h`; this document
5	defines the semantics the harness relies on.
6	
7	```c
8	typedef struct bonsai_model   bonsai_model;
9	typedef struct bonsai_context bonsai_context;
10	
11	uint32_t    bonsai_abi_version(void);       /* returns 1 */
12	const char *bonsai_last_error(void);        /* thread-local; NULL if none */
13	
14	int32_t  bonsai_model_open(const char *gguf_path, bonsai_model **out_model);
15	void     bonsai_model_close(bonsai_model *model);
16	int32_t  bonsai_n_vocab(const bonsai_model *model);
17	int32_t  bonsai_n_ctx_train(const bonsai_model *model);
18	
19	int32_t  bonsai_tokenize(const bonsai_model *model, const char *utf8,
20	                         int32_t add_bos, int32_t *ids, int32_t capacity);
21	
22	int32_t  bonsai_tensor_count(const bonsai_model *model);
23	int32_t  bonsai_tensor_info(const bonsai_model *model, int32_t index,
24	                            const char **name, int32_t *ggml_type,
25	                            int32_t *rank, int64_t ne[4]);
26	int64_t  bonsai_tensor_dequant(const bonsai_model *model, const char *name,
27	                               float *out, int64_t capacity);
28	
29	int32_t  bonsai_context_create(bonsai_model *model, int32_t n_ctx,
30	                               int32_t n_batch, bonsai_context **out_ctx);
31	void     bonsai_context_close(bonsai_context *ctx);
32	int32_t  bonsai_context_reset(bonsai_context *ctx);
33	int32_t  bonsai_eval(bonsai_context *ctx, const int32_t *tokens, int32_t n_tokens,
34	                     float *logits, int32_t logits_capacity);
35	int32_t  bonsai_generate_greedy(bonsai_context *ctx,
36	                                const int32_t *prompt, int32_t n_prompt,
37	                                int32_t n_predict, uint32_t flags,
38	                                int32_t *out_ids);
39	```
40	
41	## Build artifact
42	
43	- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` at the submission root must produce
44	  `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`.
45	- Symbols are C linkage (`extern "C"`), no C++ mangling, no extra shared
46	  libraries except the system Vulkan loader/libc. The grader checks that the
47	  library does not link llama.cpp/ggml.
48	- The library must be safe to `dlopen` without environment variables or files
49	  beside the GGUF path.
50	
51	## Model
52	
53	- `bonsai_model_open` parses the GGUF at `gguf_path`. It must not open any other
54	  model/weight file. The path is a normal filesystem path supplied by the
55	  harness.
56	- `bonsai_n_vocab` returns the vocabulary size from the GGUF tokenizer
57	  metadata.
58	- `bonsai_n_ctx_train` returns the model context length from the GGUF
59	  `context_length` metadata.
60	- Multiple models may be opened, but the tests normally use one.
61	- Errors: return a negative code and set a human-readable `bonsai_last_error`.
62	
63	## Tokenizer
64	
65	- `bonsai_tokenize` implements the model's tokenizer from the GGUF metadata:
66	  GPT-2 byte-level BPE with the `qwen35` pre-tokenizer described in
67	  `TOKENIZER.md`.
68	- `add_bos != 0` requests BOS insertion. This model's GGUF sets
69	  `tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token = false`, so the reference (`llama_tokenize`
70	  with `add_special = add_bos != 0`) does **not** prepend BOS even when
71	  `add_bos != 0`; the ids are the same as with `add_bos = 0`. The harness
72	  always calls with `add_bos = 0`.
73	- Special tokens contained in the GGUF vocabulary are matched atomically as
74	  their UTF-8 byte sequences. No chat template is applied.
75	- If `ids == NULL`, return the required number of ids without writing.
76	- If `ids != NULL` and `capacity < required`, return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
77	- The token stream must exactly match llama.cpp's tokenizer for the same flags.
78	
79	## Tensor introspection (staged tests)
80	
81	- `bonsai_tensor_count` returns the number of tensors in the GGUF.
82	- `bonsai_tensor_info` returns the tensor name (owned by the model), the numeric
83	  GGML type id (as reported by `gguf-py`), the rank, and `ne[0..3]` in **GGUF
84	  order** (`ne[0]` is the contiguous/inner dimension).
85	- `bonsai_tensor_dequant` writes the tensor to `out` as **f32** in PyTorch /
86	  safetensors row-major order: the GGUF dimensions are reversed, so `ne[0]`
87	  varies fastest and element `(i1, i0)` is at `i1*ne[0] + i0`.
88	- For PTQ1_0 the values must match the reference dequantization bit-exactly
89	  (no approximation tolerance is applied). For F32 tensors the values are
90	  copied bit-exactly.
91	- Returns the element count, or `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY` if `capacity` is too
92	  small.
93	
94	## Context and evaluation
95	
96	- `bonsai_context_create` allocates a context with `n_ctx` positions. `n_batch`
97	  is a processing hint; the engine may choose its own internal batching.
98	- `bonsai_context_reset` discards all KV/recurrent state and positions.
99	- `bonsai_eval` appends `n_tokens` token ids (n_tokens >= 1) and evaluates
100	  them. The token ids are already tokenized; the engine must not re-tokenize
101	  them.
102	- If `logits != NULL`, it must point to at least `n_vocab` floats; the engine
103	  writes the f32 logits for the **last token**. If `capacity < n_vocab`,
104	  return `BONSAI_ERR_CAPACITY`.
105	- The engine must support incremental calls: `bonsai_eval` on a prompt followed
106	  by repeated `bonsai_eval` with one token, producing the same state as one
107	  large call.
108	- Position indices advance by the number of tokens appended; reset starts at 0.
109	
110	## Greedy generation
111	
112	- `bonsai_generate_greedy` evaluates `prompt[0..n_prompt)` (may be empty), then
113	  selects the argmax token of the last-token logits, appends it, and repeats up
114	  to `n_predict` times.
115	- It writes generated token ids to `out_ids` (capacity at least `n_predict`) and
116	  returns the count. It stops early at the model's EOS token (from the GGUF
117	  tokenizer metadata) unless
118	  `BONSAI_GEN_IGNORE_EOS` is set.
119	- Determinism is required: same prompt and context size produce the same ids.
120	- After the call the context state is unspecified; the harness resets it.
121	
122	## Errors and robustness
123	
124	- `bonsai_last_error` returns a thread-local NUL-terminated string, valid until
125	  the next API call on that thread, or NULL.
126	- The library must not call `exit`, abort, or install signal handlers. Invalid
127	  arguments and allocation failures return negative codes.
128	- All API calls are made from one thread at a time. The engine may spawn worker
129	  threads internally; it must join/free them in `close`.

1	# Reference runner protocol
2	
3	`ref/bin/bonsai-ref` is a symbol-stripped llama.cpp runner (CPU and Vulkan
4	backends) for the benchmark model. It reads one command per line on stdin and
5	replies with exactly one line on stdout.
6	
7	```
8	load <model.gguf>
9	info
10	tokenize <hex-utf8> [add_bos]
11	ctx <id> <n_ctx> <cpu|vulkan>
12	reset <id>
13	eval <id> <n_tokens> <token_id>...
14	logits <id> <output.bin>
15	gen <id> <n_predict> [ignore_eos]
16	quit
17	```
18	
19	| command | reply |
20	|---|---|
21	| `load <path>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
22	| `info` | `ok arch=<arch> n_layer=<n> n_embd=<n> n_vocab=<n> n_ctx_train=<n>` |
23	| `tokenize <hex> [1]` | `ok <n> <id>...` / `error <msg>` |
24	| `ctx <id> <n_ctx> <cpu\|vulkan>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
25	| `reset <id>` | `ok` / `error <msg>` |
26	| `eval <id> <n> <id>...` | `ok` / `error <msg>` (appends and evaluates) |
27	| `logits <id> <path>` | `ok <n_vocab>`; writes raw little-endian f32 logits for the last token |
28	| `gen <id> <n> [1]` | `ok <n_generated> <id>...` (greedy; stops at EOS unless the last argument is `1`) |
29	| `quit` | exits |
30	
31	Notes:
32	
33	- `<hex-utf8>` is the lowercase hex encoding of the UTF-8 text. This avoids
34	  quoting issues. Example: `tokenize 48656c6c6f` for `Hello`.
35	- `tokenize` uses the model's `qwen35` tokenizer; `add_bos` defaults to 0.
36	- `ctx` creates a context with `n_ctx` positions. `cpu` uses `-ngl 0`;
37	  `vulkan` uses the Vulkan backend with all layers offloaded.
38	- `eval` token ids are appended to the context in order; the context must have
39	  room. Call `reset` between independent prompts.
40	- `logits` writes `n_vocab` float32 values in model-vocabulary order.
41	- `gen` selects argmax at each step and appends the token; no sampling
42	  parameters.
43	- All state is deterministic for a fixed sequence.
44	- The CPU backend is memory-bandwidth-bound on this machine: expect tens of
45	  tokens/s, versus hundreds on the Vulkan backend (and thousands for prefill).
46	  Use `cpu` for tokenizer, metadata and short spot checks; use `vulkan` for
47	  iteration. The grader compares against precomputed CPU golden values, so you
48	  do not need to run CPU inference to be graded.
49	- `ref/bin/bonsai-ref-cpu` is the same runner built without the Vulkan backend;
50	  it accepts only `cpu` contexts and is useful for pure-CPU checks.
51	
52	`llama-cli`, `llama-debug` and `llama-perplexity` are also provided for
53	ad-hoc reference runs; `llama-cli -ngl 0` uses the CPU backend and
54	`llama-cli -ngl 99` the Vulkan backend.

1	# Acceptance criteria
2	
3	The submission is this directory as you leave it. It is accepted when it builds
4	offline, implements the ABI, is correct against the CPU llama.cpp oracle, and
5	passes the VRAM gate. Performance is the optimization target and is reported
6	separately.
7	
8	## 1. Build and contract
9	
10	- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` succeeds offline in a clean container and
11	  produces `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`.
12	- The library exports the ABI in `ABI.md` and loads the GGUF path supplied by
13	  the harness.
14	- It does not read the safetensors file or any sidecar model file at runtime,
15	  does not embed model weights, does not link/execute llama.cpp or another
16	  inference engine, and does not use the network.
17	- All model computation uses Vulkan 1.4 with the compute subset of Roadmap 2026
18	  in `DEVICE.md`. "Model computation" is every arithmetic operation on model
19	  weights or activations in the forward pass (normalization, activations,
20	  softmax, RoPE, the GDN recurrence, conv1d, KV-cache updates, projections).
21	  CPU is limited to tokenization, Vulkan command/memory orchestration and I/O;
22	  CPU tensor arithmetic is a violation, including a CPU fallback.
23	- Correctness and the VRAM residency gate do not prove GPU computation: a CPU
24	  implementation with the weights resident in VRAM passes both. This is a
25	  structural requirement subject to source review; documented CPU model math
26	  makes the submission non-compliant.
27	- `ref/bin` is used only as a black box: running the documented CLI/protocol is
28	  allowed; disassembly, `strings`/`nm`/`readelf`/`objdump`, debugger use, ELF
29	  parsing or reusing the reference's code is non-compliant.
30	- No prebuilt engine binary; only source and build scripts are submitted.
31	- The grading build runs in a clean container containing only the submitted
32	  files. `data/`, `docs/` and `ref/` are not present during the build; do not
33	  read them at build time or hard-code `/workspace` paths.
34	
35	## 2. Correctness (primary)
36	
37	Hidden prompts and corpora are different from `data/samples/`. Golden values
38	are precomputed by the verifier with the CPU llama.cpp backend; grading does
39	not run CPU inference. The correctness score is a weighted mean:
40	
41	| suite | weight | metric |
42	|---|---:|---|
43	| tokenizer | 0.10 | fraction of hidden strings whose token ids match exactly |
44	| dequant | 0.15 | fraction of sampled tensors whose f32 values match the reference exactly (PTQ1_0 dequantized values widened to f32; F32 copied) and whose `tensor_info` type/rank/shape match the GGUF |
45	| logits | 0.30 | per prompt at n_ctx 512/2048/4096/8192: top-1 match, mean KL, cosine |
46	| positions | 0.15 | hidden corpus at n_ctx 512/2048: top-1 agreement and mean KL across positions |
47	| greedy | 0.30 | teacher-forced agreement over 64 steps after 64/2048/8192-token prompts (n_ctx 1024/4096/16384), plus a `generate` smoke test |
48	
49	Reference points from the CPU-vs-Vulkan llama.cpp comparison on this machine:
50	logits cosine 0.9998–0.99997, top-1 agreement 97.8–98.8%, mean KLD
51	0.0007–0.0008 nats. Greedy steps are compared teacher-forced (free-running
52	sequences diverge after the first flipped token, so sequence equality is not a
53	useful metric at long context).
54	
55	Reference (full-credit) operating points:
56	
57	- tokenizer and dequant: exact;
58	- top-1 agreement ≥ 95%;
59	- mean KL ≤ 0.01 nats;
60	- cosine similarity ≥ 0.995;
61	- teacher-forced greedy agreement ≥ 95% (and `generate` must pass its smoke
62	  test).
63	
64	The verifier converts each component into a [0,1] score and reports the suite
65	breakdown. **Acceptance requires a correctness score ≥ 0.90.** The CPU-vs-Vulkan
66	llama.cpp reference scores about 0.99 under this formula. The verifier is
67	authoritative.
68	
69	## 3. Performance (optimization target)
70	
71	Measured only after correctness acceptance:
72	
73	- pp (prompt processing): 512/2048/4096/8192-token prompts in one eval.
74	- tg (generation): 128 greedy tokens after context depths 0/512/2048/4096/8192.
75	- Reference: the stripped llama.cpp **Vulkan** binary on the same GPU, same
76	  contexts, same greedy policy, same machine.
77	- Score: geometric mean of `agent tokens/s / reference tokens/s` across the
78	  pp and tg tests. pp and tg results are reported separately.
79	- Warmup, repeated runs, and medians are used. Performance is only scored when
80	  the correctness suites pass; the perf prompts come from the hidden corpus, so
81	  they cannot be special-cased.
82	
83	## 4. VRAM (secondary acceptance gate)
84	
85	The harness polls peak process VRAM from `drm-memory-vram` in
86	`/proc/<pid>/fdinfo` (deduplicated by DRM client id) across the whole run,
87	including the largest context (n_ctx 16384), and reads peak host RSS from
88	`VmHWM`. The reference (llama.cpp Vulkan) is measured with the same workload,
89	sampling during decode.
90	
91	- Peak VRAM must satisfy
92	  `peak ≤ max(1.5 × reference_peak, reference_peak + 512 MiB)`.
93	- Peak host RSS must satisfy `peak ≤ reference_RSS + 2 GiB`.
94	- Peak VRAM must be at least ~450 MiB (half the packed model size) to
95	  demonstrate that the model is resident on the GPU rather than computed on
96	  the CPU.
97	
98	The gate is sized so that a pre-dequantized copy of the weights cannot pass;
99	the packed model must stay resident. Failing the VRAM gate sets the performance
100	score to zero; correctness is still reported. The reference peak/RSS are
101	measured by the verifier on the same GPU.
102	
103	## 5. Anti-cheat and hygiene
104	
105	- The engine must derive all weights from the GGUF at the supplied path. A
106	  submission that embeds weights, reads a generated sidecar, or depends on the
107	  safetensors file is rejected.
108	- The reference binaries are not present in the grading container; the engine
109	  may not spawn them or link llama.cpp/ggml.
110	- The submission source must be under 32 MiB (excluding `data/`, `docs/`,
111	  `ref/`, Zig build outputs, temporary files and Claude Code state); embedding
112	  model weights, a foreign engine binary or generated data is rejected. Linked
113	  libraries are checked. No network is available.
114	- The ABI permits worker threads, not child processes. The harness records
115	  `RUSAGE_CHILDREN` and live children of the grading process; a library that
116	  spawns a helper process (for example an embedded engine binary) scores zero.
117	- The engine must be deterministic for a fixed token sequence.
118	- Do not modify `data/`, `docs/`, or `ref/`.
119	
120	## 6. Deliverable notes
121	
122	The session is terminated at the deadline in `BENCH_DEADLINE_EPOCH`; only
123	workspace files present at that moment are graded. Save code and notes
124	continuously.
125	
126	Leave `NOTES.md` with:
127	
128	- the engine design and which Vulkan features it uses,
129	- known limitations and unsupported cases,
130	- measured correctness and pp/tg results,
131	- peak VRAM at the contexts you tested.

1	// Copyright 2021-2026 The Khronos Group Inc.

3	// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0
4	
5	= VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix
6	:toc: left
7	:docs: https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/
8	:refpages: https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/
9	:sectnums:
10	
11	This document proposes adding support for so-called cooperative matrix
12	operations that enables multiple shader invocations to cooperatively and
13	efficiently perform matrix multiplications.
14	
15	== Problem Statement
16	
17	A growing number of GPU applications are making use of matrix multiplication
18	operations. Modern GPU HW can take advantage of cross-invocation communication
19	channels or other hardware facilities to implement matrix multiplications
20	operations more efficiently but there is currently no suitable standard
21	SPIR-V/API mechanism to expose these features to applications or libraries.
22	
23	== Solution Space
24	
25	Applications or libraries can use subgroup primitives to write more efficient
26	matrix multiplication kernels but, while technically possible on some hardware,
27	this approach often does not make it possible to write optimal kernels and
28	requires applications to have a lot of device-specific knowledge.
29	
30	NVIDIA exposed with VK_NV_cooperative_matrix a new set of abstractions for such
31	cooperative matrix operations. These include cooperative load and store
32	instructions, a matrix multiplication-addition instruction as well a limited
33	support for element-wise operations on these matrices. Since the release of
34	that extension, a growing body of evidence in the form of discussions and
35	other similar vendor extensions suggests that this approach is suitable for
36	a wide variety of devices and applications and is thus a good candidate for
37	standardization.
38	
39	== Proposal
40	
41	Work towards a standard extension that exposes abstractions similar as those
42	released under VK_NV_cooperative_matrix.
43	
44	== Examples
45	
46	See specifications and presentations for VK_NV_cooperative_matrix.
47	
48	== Issues
49	
50	None.
51	
52

1	# Target GPU and Vulkan feature set
2	
3	The benchmark runs on one machine:
4	
5	- GPU: **AMD Radeon RX 9070** (RDNA4, `RADV GFX1201`), 16304 MiB VRAM
6	- Driver: Mesa 26.0.8 (RADV), device `apiVersion` **1.4.335**
7	- Loader: Vulkan SDK **1.4.363.0**
8	- The driver prints `radv is not a conformant Vulkan implementation, testing use only.`
9	  This is expected; it is the target device.
10	
11	The engine must target **Vulkan 1.4** and the compute-relevant subset of
12	**Vulkan Roadmap 2026**. The full profile is not implementable on this GPU; the
13	three missing items are presentation/copy/host-image features that a headless
14	inference engine does not need.
15	
16	## Full VP_KHR_roadmap_2026 gaps (not required)
17	
18	| missing item | kind |
19	|---|---|
20	| `VK_KHR_copy_memory_indirect` + `indirectMemoryCopy` | device extension/feature |
21	| `VK_KHR_present_mode_fifo_latest_ready` + `presentModeFifoLatestReady` | device extension/feature |
22	| `hostImageCopy` | Vulkan 1.4 core feature |
23	
24	The line-rasterization requirement is an OR-group; the device satisfies it via
25	rectangular/Bresenham/smooth/stippled-Bresenham. The required 2026 limits are
26	all met.
27	
28	## Required compute feature set (all supported)
29	
30	Core Vulkan 1.4 features, including:
31	
32	- `shaderFloat16`, `shaderInt8`
33	- `storageBuffer16BitAccess`, `storageBuffer8BitAccess`
34	- `shaderIntegerDotProduct` (8-bit paths accelerated)
35	- `timelineSemaphore`, `bufferDeviceAddress`, `descriptorIndexing`
36	- `scalarBlockLayout`, `vulkanMemoryModel`
37	
38	Extensions/features:
39	
40	- `VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix` (revision 2; compute stage;
41	  `cooperativeMatrix = true`)
42	- `VK_KHR_maintenance5`, `VK_KHR_maintenance7`, `VK_KHR_maintenance8`,
43	  `VK_KHR_maintenance9`
44	- `VK_KHR_shader_float_controls2`
45	- `VK_KHR_shader_expect_assume`
46	- `VK_KHR_shader_subgroup_rotate`
47	- `VK_KHR_shader_subgroup_uniform_control_flow`
48	- `VK_KHR_shader_maximal_reconvergence`
49	- `VK_KHR_shader_quad_control`
50	- `VK_KHR_shader_untyped_pointers`
51	- `VK_KHR_workgroup_memory_explicit_layout`
52	- `VK_KHR_robustness2` (`robustBufferAccess2`, `robustImageAccess2`,
53	  `nullDescriptor`)
54	- `VK_KHR_pipeline_binary`, `VK_KHR_map_memory2`
55	- `VK_KHR_shader_clock`, `VK_KHR_compute_shader_derivatives`
56	
57	The device reports `matrix cores: KHR_coopmat`, `int dot: 1`, `fp16: 1`,
58	`bf16: 1`. Cooperative matrix is supported in compute shaders; `glslc` from the
59	SDK compiles `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix` f16/f32 SPIR-V.
60	
61	## Querying the device
62	
63	`vulkaninfo` is on `PATH`. The benchmark image also provides a captured
64	`docs/device/vulkaninfo.json` (`vulkaninfo -j`), the Roadmap 2026 profile
65	(`docs/device/VP_KHR_roadmap.json`), and the roadmap appendix
66	(`docs/device/Roadmap-2026.adoc`).
67	
68	Suggested checks:
69	
70	```bash
71	vulkaninfo --summary
72	vulkaninfo | grep -i -A20 "VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan14Features"
73	glslc --version
74	spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.4 shader.spv
75	```
76	
77	## Practical notes
78	
79	- Use the SDK loader:
80	  `-I "$VULKAN_SDK/include" -L "$VULKAN_SDK/lib/VulkanLoader/lib" -lvulkan`,
81	  and run with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` including that directory.
82	- The SDK is at `$VULKAN_SDK` (`/opt/vulkan-sdk` in the benchmark image).
83	- Use `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/radeon_icd.json` if automatic
84	  ICD discovery is a problem.
85	- Validation layers are installed; `VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`
86	  is useful while developing, but disable them for performance measurements.
87	- `vkprofiles` can inspect the profile file; the exact compute feature list
88	  above is the authoritative scope for this benchmark.

# bonsai-vk implementation notes

## Design

Zig 0.17 shared library implementing the C ABI in `examples/abi/bonsai.h`.
The GGUF is parsed and mmap'd at runtime; only the supplied GGUF is opened.
PTQ1_0 packed weights are uploaded unchanged to device-local Vulkan storage.
No reference engine is linked or executed by the library. Safetensors and the
reference binaries are used only by development tools under `tools/`.

All forward-pass operations are Vulkan compute shaders: embedding decode,
explicit-sign normalized block Hadamard transforms, packed ternary projections,
RMS normalization, causal depthwise convolution, grouped gated DeltaNet state
updates, partial RoPE, gated full attention, SwiGLU feed-forward layers, residuals,
output projection, and greedy argmax. CPU work is GGUF/tokenizer parsing,
introspection-only dequantization, tokenizer BPE, uploads, command recording,
and result I/O. There is no CPU inference fallback.

Vulkan 1.4 core features and the compute-related Roadmap 2026 extensions from
DEVICE.md are queried and enabled. Device-address buffers, scalar layout,
8/16-bit storage, subgroups with an explicitly requested size of 32, and f16 KV
storage are used. A cooperative matrix prefill path is under development.

PTQ1_0 blocks contain 128 values in 28 bytes: 26 permuted base-three packed bytes
followed by an fp16 scale. Hadamard512 sign vectors and transformed-weight names
are present in GGUF metadata. Embeddings apply the inverse transform; dense
inputs apply the forward transform. DeltaNet uses raw value-head order
`group*16+key_head`, then permutes to adjacent grouped heads before its output
projection.

## Tests so far

* Offline `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`: passes, creates
  `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`.
* Tokenizer: all 15 supplied vectors and 2,033 additional multilingual,
  combining-mark, whitespace, code, and special-token strings matched the
  documented CPU reference tokenizer exactly.
* Dequant: 1,230 sampled slices (152,832 float values) across all 426 tensors
  matched the safetensors development copy bit-for-bit when widened to f32.
* `Hello`, CPU reference: logits cosine 0.999993, KL 0.000073; eight generated
  greedy ids match exactly.
* 17-token English question, CPU reference: cosine 0.999995, KL 0.000049.
* 64-token mixed English/code prefix plus 16 teacher-forced decode steps, CPU
  reference: 100% top-1 agreement, mean KL 0.000210, mean cosine 0.999988.
  Incremental one-token evaluation reproduces the prompt logits.
* Preliminary isolated decode speed about 60 tokens/s; final performance and
  VRAM measurements are pending.

## Limitations / work in progress

The architecture is specialized to this GGUF model's dimensions. Prefill
batching and final long-context validation are still being implemented. Final
measured results and remaining limitations will be recorded here before delivery.

# bonsai-vk

A Zig 0.17 Vulkan 1.4 inference library for the supplied
Ternary-Bonsai-2-4B PTQ1_0 GGUF.

## Build

Requires Zig 0.17.0, `glslc` from Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0, and the system Vulkan
loader/driver. No package downloads are needed.

```sh
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
```

The result is `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`. The SDK loader search path is included
in the library's runtime search path; callers do not need to set environment
variables. GLSL is compiled to SPIR-V during the build and embedded in the
library. Neither model data nor the reference tools are needed at build time.

## Interface

Use `examples/abi/bonsai.h`; the semantics are documented in `ABI.md`.

1. Open the GGUF with `bonsai_model_open`.
2. Tokenize UTF-8 with `bonsai_tokenize`, or supply existing token ids.
3. Create a context with `bonsai_context_create` (16,384 positions supported).
4. Append tokens with `bonsai_eval`, or use `bonsai_generate_greedy`.
5. Reset a context to reuse it; close contexts before closing their model.

Errors are negative return values with a thread-local `bonsai_last_error`.
The library follows the single-calling-thread contract. An empty generation
prompt requires previously evaluated context state.

The architecture is intentionally specialized to this model. Unsupported
architectures, incompatible tensor shapes, missing required Vulkan features,
and allocation failures return errors. There is no CPU inference fallback.

## Implementation

* Runtime GGUF parsing, exact PTQ1_0/F32 introspection, and metadata-driven
  GPT-2 byte BPE with the Qwen35 Unicode pre-tokenizer.
* Packed weights remain resident in device-local Vulkan memory.
* GPU embedding decode, explicit-sign Hadamard transforms, normalization,
  gated DeltaNet, causal convolution, partial RoPE, attention, SwiGLU,
  projections, residuals, state clearing, and greedy argmax.
* Prefill processes up to 256 tokens per layer-major batch, using KHR
  cooperative matrices and a reusable f16 scratch area for **one projection**.
* Online-softmax cooperative attention for prefill, and split-context
  attention reductions for decode. KV storage is f16; recurrent state and
  activation accumulation are f32.

See `NOTES.md` for measurements and limitations. Development checks under
`tools/` use the documented reference protocol only; the library itself never
executes helper processes or opens other weight files.

# bonsai-vk: design and verification

## Build and runtime

`zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` produces `zig-out/lib/libbonsai.so`, exporting
the ABI in `examples/abi/bonsai.h`. The implementation is Zig 0.17 plus GLSL
compute shaders. The generated Zig Vulkan declarations are checked in; no
`@cImport`, dependency fetch, reference engine, or prebuilt engine is involved.
The build compiles and embeds SPIR-V and does not read `data/`, `docs/`, or
`ref/`. A fresh source-only build in a separate directory without those three
directories passed. Runtime dependencies are only the Vulkan loader and libc.
`dlopen` and model initialization were tested with SDK/loader/ICD environment
variables removed.

Only the GGUF path supplied by the caller is opened as model data. Models are
mmap'd, parsed with checked sizes/offsets, and uploaded in their original packed
representation. Contexts retain their model so releasing a model handle before
its contexts does not destroy live GPU resources. Diagnostics are thread-local.

## GPU execution

Every forward-pass operation, including state clearing and greedy argmax, is
Vulkan compute. CPU code handles GGUF/tokenizer parsing, tokenization, resource
orchestration, uploads, and result I/O. CPU tensor dequantization is used only
by the required introspection ABI, never by inference. No CPU fallback exists.

The device requests Vulkan 1.4 and queries/enables the compute Roadmap 2026
features from DEVICE.md, including the KHR cooperative matrix, maintenance,
shader-control, untyped-pointer, robustness2, clock, derivatives and pipeline
binary extensions. Missing required features cause initialization to fail.
Shaders actually use device-address buffers, scalar layout, f32/f16 arithmetic,
8/16-bit storage, fixed 32-lane subgroups, and KHR cooperative matrices.

### Model structure

* 32 residual blocks, embedding width 2560, SwiGLU intermediate width 9216.
* 24 gated DeltaNet blocks, with four-tap causal depthwise convolution,
  16 key heads and 32 value heads of width 128, f32 recurrent state.
* Eight gated full-attention blocks with 16 query heads, four KV heads, head
  dimension 256, and 64 rotary dimensions. KV storage is f16.
* The tied embedding/output matrix and dense weights use PTQ1_0. Explicit-sign
  normalized Hadamard512 transforms come from the GGUF metadata.

PTQ1_0 has 128 elements per 28-byte block: 26 permuted packed ternary bytes and
one fp16 scale. Introspection returns raw transformed-domain tensor values,
bit-exactly. Embedding lookup applies the inverse Hadamard transform; dense
projections apply the forward transform to their inputs.

DeltaNet value heads have raw order `group*16+key_head`. After gated RMS
normalization, outputs are permuted to adjacent grouped heads before the output
projection. This ordering was recovered from GGUF metadata and documented
reference tensor traces, not binary inspection.

### Execution strategy

* Decode uses packed ternary matvec shaders sharing activations across four
  output rows per subgroup; the vocabulary projection uses eight rows.
* Prefill uses layer-major batches of up to 512 tokens. A single reusable
  45 MiB f16 scratch area expands **one projection at a time** on the GPU;
  there is never a dequantized copy of the whole model. A 64-token/64-output
  cooperative GEMM tile reuses each weight fragment across four accumulators.
* DeltaNet recurrence runs in shared memory for prefill, with subgroup partial
  reductions, and uses a parallel f32 state update for decode.
* Prefill attention uses cooperative QK/PV products and online f32 softmax.
  Decode splits attention values across up to 128 context partitions before a
  deterministic f32 reduction. Cache allocations are padded to 64 positions to
  make tail tiles safe even at non-aligned context sizes.
* All state and temporary allocations are bounded by the context/batch sizes.
  Greedy argmax breaks ties in favor of the lowest token id.

## Correctness measurements

Against the documented CPU reference (not merely the Vulkan reference):

* Tokenizer: all 15 provided vectors and 2,033 additional randomized
  multilingual/combining-mark/whitespace/code/special-token strings matched
  exactly.
* Tensor dequantization: 1,230 sampled slices, 152,832 f32 values, across all
  426 tensors matched the safetensors development copy bit-for-bit.
* Diverse logits suite: 30 prompts, including multilingual text, source code,
  chat markers, arithmetic and corpus excerpts up to 2,096 tokens; prompt logits
  plus four teacher-forced decode steps each: **149/150 top-1 matches**, mean
  KL **0.0000938 nats**, maximum KL 0.00113, mean cosine **0.999979**,
  minimum cosine 0.999836.
* 8,192-token prefix plus 64 teacher-forced steps: **100% top-1 agreement**,
  mean KL **0.00000571**, mean cosine **0.999964**.
* Eight-token free-running greedy smoke test matched the CPU reference exactly.
* Incremental evaluation, deterministic resets, capacity/argument errors,
  thread-local diagnostics, retained model lifetime, and context sizes
  1/17/65/513 were exercised through the actual C ABI.
* Debug parser fuzzing: 2,001 mutated/truncated/synthetic GGUF inputs returned
  normally without a panic or out-of-bounds failure.
* Vulkan validation layers reported no validation errors during complete
  inference and ABI tests (only the expected RADV conformance warning).

These are development tests, not an official hidden-grader score. The final
512-token internal-batch configuration is being rechecked with the same suite;
results above were measured with the same kernels at the preceding batch size.

## Performance and memory

Measured through the ABI, n_ctx=16,384, three repetitions, 128 generated tokens
with EOS ignored; medians. The comparison runner uses its documented Vulkan
backend and identical tokenized prefixes. The table below is the complete
256-token-internal-batch baseline; the final 512-token batch gave 1,211 token/s
at prompt length 512 and is undergoing the final full sweep.

| Prompt tokens | bonsai pp tok/s | reference pp tok/s | bonsai tg tok/s | reference tg tok/s |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 25.4 | 225.5 | 97.3 | 179.5 |
| 512 | 1157.0 | 2632.0 | 95.9 | 184.7 |
| 2048 | 1201.3 | 2663.8 | 91.1 | 177.8 |
| 4096 | 1191.0 | 3011.0 | 86.2 | 137.5 |
| 8192 | 1141.6 | 2752.9 | 77.4 | 131.8 |

The geometric mean ratio over the four pp lengths and five tg depths was
0.493x. Prompt length one is a short-prefix startup measurement, not a bulk pp
case. The depth-zero tg case is approximated by a one-token initial prefix.

Observed baseline peak VRAM was **1,618 MiB**, versus **3,041 MiB** for the
reference; the acceptance bound from that reference peak is **4,561 MiB**.
The final larger batch has measured about **1,720 MiB**, also comfortably below
that bound. Peak host RSS was about **1,028 MiB**, versus **2,038 MiB** reference
(and an allowed bound of 4,086 MiB). The packed model remains resident on the
GPU throughout inference.

## Limitations

* Inference is specialized to this model's dimensions, quantization and
  architecture; incompatible models are rejected instead of misinterpreted.
* One sequence per context; no sampling beyond greedy generation or chat
  template application. An empty generation prompt requires prior evaluated
  state.
* Context length 16,384 is tested. Larger requests are permitted up to the
  training length, but are untested and can fail device allocation.
* f16 KV/activation conversion and reduction order differ from the CPU oracle;
  logits are tolerance-equivalent, not bit-identical. Tensor introspection is
  bit-identical.
* The implementation is slower than the highly optimized reference. Prefill
  projection bandwidth and the sequential DeltaNet recurrence remain the main
  optimization opportunities.
